The Bravery of Hadhrat Abu Dujaana Simaak bin Harasha (RA) from the Ansaar
Hadhrat Abu Dujaana (RA) Takes a Sword from Rasulullaah ﷺ and Fulfils its Rights During the Battle of Uhud

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ took hold of a sword during the Battle of Uhud and announced, "Who will take this sword from me?" When several Sahabah (RA) took the sword to have a look at it, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "(I am not giving it for looking) Who will take this sword and fulfil it rights." This made everyone hesitate and it was Hadhrat Abu Dujaana Simaak bin Harasha (RA) who said, "I shall take it and fulfil its rights." He then used it to efficiently kill the Mushrikeen.[^2]

Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA) narrates that that Rasulullaah ﷺ took hold of a sword during the Battle of Uhud and announced, "Who will take this sword and fulfil its rights." It was Hadhrat Abu Dujaana Simaak bin Harasha (RA) who said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I shall take it and fulfil its rights, but what are its rights?" Rasulullaah ﷺ then handed the sword over to him and he left. Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) says that he followed Hadhrat Abu Dujaana (RA) and (saw that) he destroyed everything he used the sword on. He eventually came across some Mushrikeen women at the foot of the mountain. Amongst them was Hind who was reciting the following couplets (to incite the Mushrikeen men, which meant):

"We are the daughters of prominent people
Who walk on exquisite cushions
We wear musk on our heads
And are ready to embrace you when you arrive
We shall however separate from you if you flee the battlefield
Separate in a manner after which there shall be no reconciliation"

When Hadhrat Abu Dujaana (RA) intended to attack her (because she was an active participant in the battle), she started calling (for help) to the battlefield. However, no one came to her assistance. He then left her. Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) said to him, "I have been extremely impressed by everything I have seen you do besides the fact that you did not kill that woman." Hadhrat Abu Dujaana (RA) said, "When no one responded to her call for help, I did not want the sword of Rasulullaah ﷺ to strike a helpless woman."[^3]

Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) narrates, "During the Battle of Uhud, Rasulullaah ﷺ took hold of a sword and announced, 'Who will take this sword with its rights.' I said, 'I shall, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' Rasulullaah ﷺ ignored me and again
